external_entities.name: Member
external_entities.description: A person who uses the loyalty platform, collects points, and spends them on gift cards.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.
external_entities.notes: The text does not identify individual members by name.

external_entities.name: Member phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone on which the mobile app keeps a refresh token.
external_entities.notes: The phone is outside the system's cloud account.

external_entities.name: Partner app
external_entities.description: A web application operated by another company on its own server.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
external_entities.notes: The text gives the meal-planning service as an example of a partner app.

external_entities.name: Browser
external_entities.description: A browser used by a member to sign in and approve partner-app consent.
external_entities.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where the browser runs.

processes.name: Mobile app
processes.description: The loyalty mobile application that signs members in, receives access tokens, and calls the rewards API.
processes.notes: The text does not say whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: Authorization server
processes.description: The authorization server that authenticates members, handles authorization-code flows, issues tokens, and maintains partner consents.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: The authorization server signs tokens for both the rewards API and the support console. Its sign-in idle timeout is not decided.

processes.name: Rewards API
processes.description: The API that accepts access tokens and reads and writes the points ledger.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: The API does not check which client or audience a token was issued for. It downloads a public verification key at startup.

processes.name: Partner app
processes.description: A partner web application that obtains authorization and can show a member's points.
processes.source_excerpt: such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points
processes.notes: This process corresponds to the partner app external entity and represents the application behaviour described in the source.

processes.name: Support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: Identity database
data_stores.description: The database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_stores.notes: The database also contains authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents. The source does not say how it is protected at rest.

data_stores.name: Points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction
data_stores.notes: The ledger records which client made each change, but not which member approved it. The source does not say how it is protected at rest.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store receiving every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
data_stores.notes: The source does not say how the log store is protected at rest.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.
data_flows.data_description: Member interactions with the loyalty mobile app

data_flows.name: authorize member
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in using the authorization code flow and receives an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: The source does not state whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.
data_flows.data_description: Member authorization request and authorization tokens

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.notes: The access token is a plain bearer token valid for one hour.

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests to the authorization server using its client secret.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: The partner app's client secret is sent in the request body. Every partner app receives every scope.
data_flows.data_description: Client credentials, authorization requests, and tokens

data_flows.name: use browser
data_flows.description: A member uses a browser to sign in and approve partner-app consent.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

data_flows.name: sign in and consent
data_flows.description: The browser accesses the authorization server's sign-in page and submits member consent.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen that lists the scopes
data_flows.notes: The authorization-server sign-in is kept in a cookie for thirty days; no idle timeout was decided.
data_flows.data_description: Member credentials, sign-in session, and consented scopes

data_flows.name: return authorization code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: Authorization codes remain valid for ten minutes.

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: A partner app calls the rewards API to show a member's points.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a meal-planning service that shows a member's points

data_flows.name: obtain access token
data_flows.description: The support console obtains or uses access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account. It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: Closing an account does not remove that member's refresh tokens.

data_flows.name: manage identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and manages member identities, credentials, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_flows.notes: This includes deleting a partner app's refresh token when a member disconnects it.
data_flows.data_description: Member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: manage points ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes balances and points transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
data_flows.notes: Redeeming points for a gift card requires a valid access token carrying the redeem scope.

data_flows.name: write API requests
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes each received request and its headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

trust_boundaries.name: Own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The system components and stores that run in the organisation's own cloud account.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: Members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: The members' phones, which are outside the organisation's cloud account.

trust_boundaries.name: Partner apps' own servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers operated by other companies that host partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database is confidential because it contains member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly lists personal data and authentication credentials stored in the identity database.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger is confidential because it contains member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly states that the ledger holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store is confidential because it retains all requests and headers, which may contain request and authentication data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every rewards API request, headers included, is written to the API log store.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on the same public hostname as the support console.
assumptions.basis: The source says the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The authorization server is internet-facing because members and browsers access its sign-in page and partner applications use its token endpoints.
assumptions.basis: The source describes browser sign-in and partner-app token requests to the authorization server.
